summary: Iteration 3 retest of the 4 fixes plus a UI regression check. Used 2 real full product-prices runs (1 backend, 1 UI) and real /api/rewrite calls. Fix 1 PASS: scores match the verdicts (Outdated 6/8/6, Uncertain 40/45/55, Current 96), and the gauge now reads 30 or 28 'Stale' (was 61). Fix 2 PASS: for the PS5 claim, sources[0] is the 2026-03-27 PlayStation price-change post. btn-copy-fix-c2 and corrected source [1] both point to it. Netflix sources[0] is help.netflix.com 'Plans and Pricing'. Fix 3 PASS: rewrites stay grammatical with citations before the final period, e.g. '...$599.99 effective April 2, 2026 [1][2], and the base iPhone 15 starts at $799. ...$19.99 per month in the United States [3][4].' Fix 4 PASS: an intercepted 200 SSE stream with only meta + claims shows error-state ('The connection closed before the check finished. Please try again.'), a toast, and Try again. Regression PASS: route-badge 'Direct', gauge and counts, 4 claim cards, 2 copy-fix buttons with source text in the clipboard, Copy corrected answer (toast, Sources list in the clipboard, button becomes 'Regenerate & copy'), and Run details (header counts calls and tokens; the toggle shows rows; a rewrite row is added after Copy corrected). No console errors.

minor.issue: Verdicts vary between runs. 'ChatGPT Plus costs $20' was Current 96 in one run and Uncertain 55 in the next (only third-party sources were found). iPhone 15 $799 is Uncertain because the evidence is only from 2023. This is not a code bug; it's an observation.

ui_bugs.issue: When the stream ends early, the error-state appears correctly, but the partial results stay below it: the gauge shows '–' / 'No claims' while a pending, pulsing highlight remains for the claim that was received. Consider hiding the results overview or marking pending claims as failed on error.

action_items: Optional: on a stream error, clear or mark the partial 'Checking' state (gauge 'No claims' plus a pending highlight)
critical_code_review_comments: verify_claim score clamp is correct. Note: if the model returns verdict 'Current' with a low score, it is forced up to >=70, and the opposite for Outdated. Fine, given the verdict is authoritative.

If the LLM returns no valid source_ids, the code falls back to all results in Tavily order, so a stale source can still come first in that case. Possibly sort the fallback by published_date (often None, though).
freshcheck.js streamCheck: the 'finished' flag is set before the data check, so a 'done' event with malformed data would still count. Edge case only.
context_for_next_testing_agent: No auth, no DB. Real product-prices check takes about 6-15s. Testids: corrected-answer-text, corrected-source-{n}, run-log-row-{i}, card-claim-cN, link-source-cN-k, btn-copy-fix-cN, gauge-overall-score (gauge-score-value is SVG; use inner_text on gauge-overall-score). Run with: export REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=... && pytest tests/test_freshcheck_iter3.py -n 0.
